title: Movimiento del Sombrero Profits From Manzo’s Murder, His Brother Charges
author: Álvaro Delgado Gómez
content:
_This article by Álvaro Delgado Gómez originally appeared in the[August 4,
2026 edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4848753/movimiento-del-
sombrero-lucra-con-asesinato-de-manzo-acusa-su-hermano-entrevista/)._

**Mexico City, August 3 (SinEmbargo).–** The Movimiento del Sombrero and the
Mayor of Uruapan, Grecia Quiroz, have turned the murder of Carlos Manzo into a
political discourse for electoral purposes and have obstructed the
clarification of the case by not fully cooperating with the authorities,
charged Juan Manzo, brother of the former mayor and undersecretary of
Government of Michoacán.

In an interview with Álvaro Delgado on the program “Los Periodistas” broadcast
through SinEmbargo Al Aire’s YouTube channel, Juan Manzo maintained that the
priority should be to clarify his brother’s murder and not turn the case into
a political banner heading into the 2027 elections, a process in which Grecia
Quiroz has already confirmed she will seek the governorship backed by the
Movimiento del Sombrero.

> “It is more profitable for them not to deliver results, in order to
> politicize the absence of results. And it seems to me that in the case of
> the Movimiento del Sombrero **they have used Carlos’s case, who is
> ultimately the greatest victim of this regrettable event, so that his death
> becomes a political discourse** ,” he stated.

Carlos Manzo was murdered on November 1, 2025, during the Festival de las
Velas. To date, the authorities have made dozens of arrests over the alleged
participation of members of organized crime, officials and members of his
security detail.**The most recent progress came at the end of July with the
arrest in Jalisco of Ramón Ángel “N,” alias “El R1,” identified by the
authorities as the alleged intellectual and financial author of the murder and
leader of a cell linked to the Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG).** In
the same operation, Jesús Salvador “N,” “El Chuy,” was captured.

With these arrests, the federal Government reported that 31 people are now
detained in connection with the case, among them criminal operators, alleged
recruiters, officials and escorts of the Mayor himself, while the
investigations continue to determine all responsibilities in the planning and
execution of the crime.

Juan Manzo asserted in the interview that, beyond directly solving the crime,
the political group to which his brother belonged would have the obligation to
provide any information that helps the authorities clarify the facts. **“It is
not that they are going to solve it, it is simply having the will to
cooperate, having the will to present the elements within their reach in order
to uncover the context in which the crime could have developed,” he noted.**

In that regard, he criticized that the arrest of José Manuel Jiménez,
identified by him as a member of the Movimiento del Sombrero, had not been
supported either, as well as the defense of other members of the group who
face proceedings related to the case.

Juan Manzo also questioned the conduct of Grecia Quiroz, considering that she
has fallen into contradictions regarding the available information about the
threats that Carlos Manzo allegedly received before being murdered.

> “If Grecia says that Carlos had threats, well those threats must be on the
> phones, and she does not want to hand over the phones. So there is a
> contradiction that she does not want to clear up because it is easier to
> point at those who are her opposition within this political struggle,” he
> maintained.

For the undersecretary, clarifying the murder must take precedence over any
electoral aspiration. “Beyond the political struggle we must clarify the
Carlos Manzo case, and each person will afterward have their right to
participate legitimately in the elections,” he expressed.

Asked directly whether he believes that the Mayor of Uruapan and the
Movimiento del Sombrero are profiting from the murder of Carlos Manzo, he
responded in the affirmative.

> “It is regrettable, but that is how it is, they profit from a tailored
> narrative with Carlos’s tragedy. I believe they have not acted with
> transparency,” he stated.

He added that those who truly seek justice should give priority to the
investigations advancing without obstacles and without protecting people close
to the movement.

> “For those who are truly pained by the loss of Carlos, beyond the political,
> the most just thing is that it find total clarity and that there be no
> impunity,” he said.

He even warned that the political identity of some of those involved could
become a factor for obstructing justice.

> “Being from the Movimiento del Sombrero can become an element of impunity
> for the very crime against Carlos Manzo, and I am not going to accept that.
> Nor if there is impunity on the part of a member of Morena or another
> party,” he asserted.

Finally, Juan Manzo maintained that there is a strategy to turn the case into
a tool of electoral profitability.

> “There is a narrative that sees its interests affected in countless places
> where it seeks to participate. There are points where this narrative is used
> to obtain electoral profitability,” he concluded.

**Grecia Quiroz assumed the municipal presidency of Uruapan after the murder
of Carlos Manzo. In recent months she confirmed that she will seek the
governorship of Michoacán in 2027 backed by the Movimiento del Sombrero, with
which her husband won the mayoralty through the independent route.** In
addition, she registered with the Mexican Institute of Industrial Property
(IMPI) the trademarks “Carlos Manzo” and “Movimiento Independiente del
Sombrero,” which since the beginning of 2026 she can use to organize meetings,
consultancies and political activities.

Since taking office, Quiroz has blamed state and federal authorities for the
lack of security that, she maintains, her husband faced before being murdered.
This past May she questioned that the federal Government granted protection to
the Governor on leave of Sinaloa, Rubén Rocha Moya, while she claimed that
Carlos Manzo was “ignored” despite belonging to a citizens’ movement.

The murder investigation has also been accompanied by public differences
between the Mayor and Juan Manzo.

The undersecretary of Government has accused her of not handing over his
brother’s cell phone so that it can be reviewed by the Prosecutor’s Office, of
trying to favor the release of detained escorts, and of the City Council
paying for their defense.

Quiroz has rejected those accusations, asserted that the phone is available
for the proceedings as long as the review is carried out in her presence, and
denied that the municipal Government covers the fees of the escorts’ lawyers.

    
    
    Álvaro Delgado Gómez is a journalist born in Lagos de Moreno, Jalisco, in 1966. He began his career as a reporter in 1986 and has worked in the newsrooms of _El Financiero_ , _El Nacional_ , and _El Universal_. In November 1994, he joined the weekly magazine _Proceso_ as a reporter, where he served as Head of Political News and specialized in political coverage. He has authored several books, most notably _El Yunque, la ultraderecha en el poder_ (Plaza y Janés), _El Ejército de Dios_ (Plaza y Janés), and _El engaño. Prédica y práctica del PAN_ (Grijalbo). His most recent book is _El amasiato. El pacto secreto Peña-Calderón y otras traiciones panistas_ (Editorial Proceso).
